> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b53571d760d707d54d42c650023a824000c6335a` — the merge of head `4a7e194f97700d6f0a1d91f142c930ce1afd9608` into base `babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b53571d760d707d54d42c650023a824000c6335a && git checkout b53571d760d707d54d42c650023a824000c6335a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84 4a7e194f97700d6f0a1d91f142c930ce1afd9608 && git checkout -B drift-repro babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84 && git merge --no-ff 4a7e194f97700d6f0a1d91f142c930ce1afd9608

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b0796f023975cbdb2563e8a3ae55f6832afcb72a`
Local-runs: probe — downloaded the pinned better-auth and @better-auth/sso 1.7.12 tarballs (npm pack, scripts ignored) to read the vendor source the module headers cite; nothing built or run
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts + read in the cited code: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-in-options.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts, docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md (D6), content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx

### ① Derived judgments

- Implicit link through an SSO source, verification on: the accept-set narrows to an asserted address at a listed, verified domain, by equality (`refuseImplicitAccountLink`, rule 4). Right: it is the matching rule `sso.mdx` and ADR-0135 D6 already publish for creation, read through the same module.
- Sign-in through an SSO source into a linked account, verification on: an asserted address other than the account's own is admitted only at a proven domain (`refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`). Right where the sign-in would change the stored address; its reach beyond that is ④ finding 2.
- Refusal surface: no new error code. `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` is reused with two rule-level descriptions that name no domain; the error-code ledger and `packages/spec` are untouched. Right.
- `readSsoProviderProvenDomains` extraction: the creation rule reads the same inputs and answers the same verdicts as on `main`. Right, behaviour unchanged.
- `ImplicitLinkGateOptions.provenDomain` becomes required and `LinkingAuthContext` gains an optional `email`: both internal to the package, one caller, updated in the diff. No published type moves. Right.
- Verification off, a non-SSO source, an explicit link and a sign-in asserting the account's own address return before any provider read and before any throw. Right, and it matches the Unchanged list.
- Fail closed: an unreadable provider row refuses; an unreadable account throws, which the vendor gate answers as a refusal. Both sit behind the verification switch. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: 58 runs, 39 success, 19 skipped, none failed or pending; the two timeouts reported from the local sweep do not appear on the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no stored shape changes). This is the level AGENTS.md sets for a non-protocol breaking change. The title carries `!` and the migration text names who moves. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (an address asserted at sign-in is refused even where the sign-in would not change the stored address): escalated, not closed here. See ④ finding 2. The tree and the PR's own prose agree with each other; the authority for that reach is not on any record this review can read.
- Two nearby open drafts touching the `implicit-account-linking.ts` header and another section of `sso.mdx`: textual only, no gate code. Answered, no action on this head.
- The two local battery timeouts: answered by the head's check-runs, all green.

### ④ Design judgment

Where an SSO sign-in links to an existing account, or would change a linked account's stored address, the PR makes the published proven-domain rule real on paths where it did not yet hold: the spec's own refusal applied at the remaining entries, not a capability taken away. It is breaking for deployments with verification on, and the changeset says so. Attempts to get past the guard (link and sign-in paths, SAML and OIDC, verification off, explicit link, own-address sign-in) found no way through.

1. should-fix — `docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md`, D6. On `main` it says accounts that already exist are not re-checked; after this PR the tree re-checks them on a link and on an asserted address. Required: a dated note on D6 recording the extension and the ruling that authorises it, as the existing D6 note records the creation rule. It is a governed path, so it lands by its own route; it must be tracked against this PR before merge.
2. should-fix — `refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`. The function judges the address a sign-in asserts whether or not that sign-in would change what the account holds. The rule as the title and changeset title state it ("changes its email address") is fully kept by refusing only a sign-in that would change the address; the wider refusal removes sign-ins that `main` and ADR-0135 D6 declare unchanged and protects no stored state. Required, one of: (a) the ruling that states the rule on the assertion is put on record (the D6 note of finding 1 is the place), and `sso.mdx` and the changeset say plainly that the sign-in is refused on the asserted address even when the stored address would stay as it is; or (b) the function judges only a sign-in that would change the address. Without (a), (b) is the reading the published spec supports.
3. nit — `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` and the changeset "Who moves" list: a link at a domain the provider does not list at all was already refused on `main` by the existing link refusal; only the listed-domain subdomain case moves. State the two cases apart. Prose only.
4. nit — tests: the address rule is pinned end to end for OIDC with the provider set to update the account; there is no end-to-end case over SAML and none for a provider that does not update the account (the case finding 2 turns on). Follow-up card.
5. nit — the comments at the SSO mount in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` and on `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled` still describe the rule for creation only. Follow-up.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 earn a delta review of their fix by this seat.

## Maintainer ruling: reach of the SSO proven-domain rule on sign-in

Ruling-ref: decision card cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XCikvpxecbhFuSpfkcUCAG2, option labelled 「B：只拦会改邮箱的登录」, chosen by Leehom on 2026-11-14.

**Rule.** With SSO domain verification on, a sign-in into an already-linked account is refused by the proven-domain rule only when that sign-in would change the stored address; where that cannot be determined, it is refused. A sign-in that reports an address outside the proven domains but changes nothing is admitted, as on `main`. The creation rule and the implicit-link rule are unchanged.

**Bearing on this PR.** Delta record 6882064855 at head `ba3fd25ea8` already reads this rule in the tree: round-1 finding 2 closed by option (b), and the end-to-end case for a provider that does not update the account exists. No code change is owed for the ruling. Still open on this head, prose and comments only: nits 6, 7 and 8 of that record. The PR body should state this rule and cite this ruling before landing, since the squash message comes from it.

**Bearing on #33356.** The ADR-0135 D6 note may name this ruling as its authority, which answers finding 1 of record 6882817474 by its option (a). Finding 2 of that record (an implicit link, not every link) is still owed. This seat delta-reviews #33356 after the fix.

**Caveat.** If the security lane holds a reason that the narrow rule is not enough, it says so and the question returns to the maintainer before this PR lands.
